title: Permit v1 → Control Framework Mappings
description: Mapping from Permit v1 wire-format fields and audit-export-bundle artifacts to specific control IDs in major AI / security / privacy frameworks. Auditor-and-procurement-friendly: a buyer reads which Permit fields satisfy which control evidence requirements. Honesty over coverage: 'sufficient' / 'partial' / 'necessary' labels reflect the actual evidentiary weight of the field for that control.

nist_ai_rmf.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
nist_ai_rmf.official_citation: NIST AI 100-1 — Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), January 2023
nist_ai_rmf.scope: Voluntary framework for AI risk management
nist_ai_rmf.id_format: FUNCTION CATEGORY.SUBCATEGORY (e.g., GOVERN 1.1, MAP 2.3, MEASURE 2.9, MANAGE 1.1) — note: official format uses spaces between FUNCTION and category, periods within category.subcategory; no hyphens

functions.GOVERN: A culture of risk management is cultivated and present (cross-cutting; infused throughout the other functions)
functions.MAP: Context is recognized and risks related to context are identified
functions.MEASURE: Identified risks are assessed, analyzed, or tracked
functions.MANAGE: Risks are prioritized and acted upon based on a projected impact

nist_ai_rmf.verification: Functions and key Categories/Subcategories within GOVERN, MAP, and MEASURE verified verbatim against NIST AI 100-1 official PDF (2026-05-10 WebFetch). MANAGE function structure not exhaustively read in this pass but is consistent with the four-function framework structure documented above. Subcategory IDs cited in mappings below are from the official NIST publication.

controls.rationale: Risk assessment must identify the individuals who provided the information for the assessment; permit id provides traceability to specific decisions whose evidence is referenced.
Unique permit identifier supports incident reconstruction; not sufficient on its own.
Tenancy boundary identifier supports demonstrating logical access controls between tenants.

For ADMT used in significant decisions per §7150(b)(3), the risk assessment must identify the output of the ADMT and how the business will use the output to make a significant decision. The permit's decision field IS that output.
Article 12 logging requires recordkeeping of AI system events; the decision is the central event.
Provides human-readable narrative supporting the documentation of ADMT logic; structured decision_details is the more rigorous evidence.
The decision_details code + reason captures the ADMT's logic at evaluation time, including assumptions/limitations expressed as policy rules.
Documents the actions the ADMT system takes based on the decision output.
Supports verification of consumer requests; subject identifier is the binding from a permit to a verifiable consumer.
Identifies the subject for access-control audit purposes.
Action name supports identifying the purpose for processing; full purpose documentation is broader and lives in policy_id/policy_version.
Identifies the third party (AI provider) to whom the business discloses or makes available consumers' personal information for processing.
Deployer obligation to use AI systems as instructed; identifying the specific provider/model is necessary to match against the provider's instructions.
Supports identifying the scale of processing (approximate consumer count and per-decision data volume).
Cryptographic fingerprint of stable request semantics enables tamper-detection and replay verification.
Automatic logging of AI events; fingerprint is part of the event record.
Cryptographic binding of the dispatched request to the permit decision supports policies/procedures ensuring ADMT works as intended (i.e., no covert request alteration).
Evidence that the request as evaluated matches the request as dispatched is foundational to event integrity in the logging requirement.
Idempotency keys support deduplication and replay-safety of automated operations.

Policy version stamp identifies the specific policies/procedures the business has implemented to ensure ADMT works as intended; combined with policy diff tracking, supports change-management evidence.
Policy version on every decision enables traceability to a specific change-management record.
Timestamp drives retention-period calculation; risk assessment must document retention period and criteria. Combined with retention engine, supports the §7155 timing requirements.
Article 26(6) requires high-risk AI deployer logs to be kept ≥6 months; created_at is the anchor for that retention window.
Permit timestamp supports the retention defense under deletion-exception carve-outs (security/integrity per (d)(2); legal-obligation retention per (d)(8)).
Lineage supports documenting the business's planned method for collecting/using/disclosing personal information across multi-step automated workflows.
Lifecycle status (evaluated, bound, dispatched, closed, expired, revoked) supports tracing incident scope to specific permit lifecycle stages.

controls.rationale: Risk assessments must be retained, reviewed and updated at least every 3 years. Signed export bundle is a tamper-evident retention artifact supporting that obligation.
Provides the cryptographically verifiable retention substrate for high-risk AI deployer logs to be kept under deployer control for ≥6 months.

audit_export_bundle_mappings.artifact: RFC 3161 timestamp receipt anchored to integrity checkpoint

controls.rationale: Independent third-party time witness supports nonrepudiation claims about when events occurred.

Listed safeguard for risk assessments includes encryption, segmentation, access controls, change management, network monitoring, and data and integrity monitoring. Hash chain is data-integrity monitoring evidence.

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
permit_evidence: policy_id + policy_version stamp every Permit with the regulatory framework the policy was authored against
Signed audit exports provide tamper-evident documentation that decisions complied with the stated policy

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
permit_evidence: policy_id + policy_version + permit decision_details establish the transparent connection from policy → decision
Hash chain provides tamper-evident outcomes

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.
permit_evidence: Replay drift taxonomy enables ongoing monitoring of whether policy decisions remain consistent over time
Audit exports provide the artifact for periodic review

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
permit_evidence: resource_provider + resource_model on every Permit forms a queryable inventory of every AI system the organization has used
permit lineage (parent_permit_id + delegation_depth) tracks compositional AI system use

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.
permit_evidence: Every Permit is documentation of an evaluated AI use; decision_details captures the risk-relevant context
Audit exports are the broader-communication artifact

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party's intellectual property or other rights.
permit_evidence: resource_provider identifies the third-party AI vendor; routing decisions track multi-vendor exposure
Closure records bind to specific vendor responses, enabling third-party-attributable evidence

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented.
permit_evidence: subject_type + subject_id + action_name + project_id together document the intended-use context for every AI invocation
policy_id captures the context-specific laws/norms encoded as policy

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making decisions and taking subsequent actions.
permit_evidence: decision_details captures the AI system's reasoning and limits at decision time
actions_json documents how the output is used; closure record binds the actual output

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components — as identified in the MAP function — are monitored when in production.
permit_evidence: Every production AI call produces a Permit; closure record binds actual production behavior
Replay enables continuous-monitoring comparison of intended vs actual decisions

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: AI system security and resilience — as identified in the MAP function — are evaluated and documented.
permit_evidence: Hash chain + Ed25519 signed exports provide cryptographic evidence of integrity (security)
RFC 3161 timestamped checkpoints provide tamper-evident time-witness (resilience)

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Risks associated with transparency and accountability — as identified in the MAP function — are examined and documented.
permit_evidence: Audit exports + offline verifier provide vendor-independent transparency
Three trust-root channels (Keel API, PyPI, GitHub) make accountability evidence verifiable post-vendor

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context — as identified in the MAP function — to inform responsible use and governance.
permit_evidence: decision_details + closure record document the model output within its decision context
Replay validates that the documented decision still reproduces under the recorded snapshot

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Fairness and bias — as identified in the MAP function — are evaluated and results are documented.
permit_evidence: Replay drift detection identifies whether decisions become biased over time
Audit exports retain the evaluation evidence under cryptographic integrity

nist_ai_rmf.verbatim: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts.
permit_evidence: Replay drift taxonomy provides systematic tracking of decision changes
Permits + closure records compare intended (decision) vs actual (closure) AI performance

owasp_llm_2025.name: Prompt Injection
permit_evidence: binding_request_hash binds the canonical wire-body bytes at dispatch time; any post-decision request alteration (including prompt injection that mutates the request payload after the policy decision) is cryptographically detectable
request_fingerprint stable semantic fingerprint detects semantic-level prompt manipulation across the request lifecycle

owasp_llm_2025.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
permit_evidence: Permit decision can deny or constrain operations that would disclose sensitive information before execution
Audit exports provide post-incident forensic evidence of what sensitive content (if any) was processed and through which provider

owasp_llm_2025.name: Supply Chain
permit_evidence: resource_provider + resource_model identify the specific AI supply-chain component used for each decision
Permit policy_id can encode supply-chain governance rules (allowlist of providers, model versions, etc.)

owasp_llm_2025.name: Improper Output Handling
permit_evidence: Closure record's client_response_digest_v1 binds the bytes actually delivered to the client, enabling post-hoc validation that output handling was correct
Replay drift detection identifies if output validation behavior has changed

owasp_llm_2025.name: Excessive Agency
permit_evidence: Permit primitive is the pre-execution authorization for every agent action — agency is bounded by policy, not by the LLM's autonomous capabilities
actions_json + constraints_json define the bounds of authorized agency for each decision
Permit lineage (parent_permit_id, delegation_depth) tracks delegated agency across multi-step workflows

owasp_llm_2025.name: System Prompt Leakage
permit_evidence: binding_request_hash detects if the system prompt portion of the request differs at dispatch from what was authorized at decision time

owasp_llm_2025.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
permit_evidence: Audit exports retain the resource_inputs_json (which may include reference to embedding/vector inputs) for forensic review
Replay drift detection may identify if vector-retrieval behavior has changed over time

owasp_llm_2025.name: Misinformation
permit_evidence: Closure record + replay provide post-hoc auditability of what the LLM actually output and under what decision context
Permit decision_details + audit exports help establish ground-truth narrative for misinformation incidents

owasp_llm_2025.name: Unbounded Consumption
permit_evidence: Permit budgets_json + constraints_json enforce per-call consumption limits at pre-execution
actual_input_tokens + actual_output_tokens + actual_cost_usd_micros provide consumption telemetry; usage_ledger supports budget reconciliation

soc2_category_level.note: Mapping is at the CATEGORY level (CC1 through CC9). Sub-criterion verbatim text was not directly verified in this pass due to AICPA gating; confirm sub-criterion IDs and verbatim from the AICPA TSC 2017 (with 2022 revisions) document before customer-facing publication.

mappings.permit_evidence: Permit decision + risk-assessment evidence in audit exports support CC3 control activities. Sub-criterion alignment likely CC3.1 (risk identification) and CC3.2 (risk analysis); verify.

mappings.category: CC6 Logical and Physical Access Controls
mappings.permit_evidence: Permit subject_type + subject_id + RBAC integration support CC6 user identification and access control evidence. Sub-criterion alignment likely CC6.1 (access controls), CC6.2 (user provisioning), CC6.6 (authentication); verify.

Hash chain + signed exports + RFC 3161 timestamps support CC7 monitoring and logging evidence. Sub-criterion alignment likely CC7.1 (detection of vulnerabilities/anomalies), CC7.2 (monitoring), CC7.3 (anomaly evaluation); verify.
policy_id + policy_version stamping on every decision provides change-management traceability per AI decision. Sub-criterion alignment likely CC8.1 (change authorization, testing, approval); verify.

Permit constraints_json + budgets_json + denial decisions provide pre-execution risk mitigation; replay drift detection supports CC9 ongoing risk mitigation review. Sub-criterion alignment likely CC9.1 (risk mitigation activities); verify.

iso_42001_clause_level.note: Mapping is at the CLAUSE level (Clauses 4 through 10 + Annex A) per the standard form of ISO management system standards. Verbatim clause titles and Annex A control IDs/titles are paywalled at iso.org and were NOT directly verified in this pass. Verify against the purchased standard or audit firm copy before customer-facing publication.

mappings.permit_evidence: Permit policy_id + policy_version stamps demonstrate planned AI use is documented; AI objectives and risk treatment are encoded in policy. Sub-clause alignment likely 6.1 (actions to address risks) and 6.2 (AI objectives); verify.

Permit primitive itself IS the operational artifact of the AI Management System — every operational AI use produces tamper-evident evidence. Sub-clause alignment likely 8.1 (operational planning and control); verify.
Audit exports + replay drift detection support Clause 9 performance evaluation. Sub-clause alignment likely 9.1 (monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation) and 9.3 (management review); verify.
Replay drift + permit lineage + policy diff tracking support continuous improvement evidence. Sub-clause alignment likely 10.1 (nonconformity and corrective action); verify.

Verbatim Annex A control IDs (typically A.2 through A.10 with subcontrols) were not directly verified in this pass due to ISO paywall. Annex A controls covering 'AI system documentation,' 'AI system operations records,' and 'third-party AI risk' are likely the most directly applicable; verify against the standard or audit firm copy.

explicit_non_mappings.rationale: Proposed-text trigger 'operation of generative models, such as large language models' was REMOVED in the September 2025 final adopted text. Do not cite as a current trigger. Final scope is limited to ADMT used to REPLACE human decisionmaking for significant decisions (§7150(b)(3)) or training ADMT for those uses or for identity-biological-profiling tech (§7150(b)(6)).

ADMT 'quality of personal information' sub-block (completeness/representativeness/timeliness/validity/accuracy/consistency/reliability) was removed from §7152(a)(2) in the final adopted text. Final §7152(a)(2) only requires identifying categories of personal information processed.

The detailed ADMT evaluation framework with three sub-requirements in proposed (a)(6)(B)(i)–(iii) was reduced to a single line at final §7152(a)(6)(A)(iv): 'Implementing policies, procedures, and training to ensure that the business's ADMT works for the business's purpose and does not unlawfully discriminate based upon protected characteristics.'
